claims.reasoning: The historical censored two-pass bootstrap remains the same scope and budget; its timeout is not diagnosed as an FFI failure. This successor preserves the locked synchronization, registry reader, retirement and arity fixes, and adds explicit foreign-call frame leases in all three SFUN macro families and close-before-retire/cleanup admission. The observed official FFI roundtrip previously lost its return destination after processor retirement. The source candidate rejects removal of an origin while its native caller owns a frame and retains a busy VM rather than destroying it. Ordinary run markers are not counted as foreign frames. The finite protocol models cover split admission, saturation and cleanup rollback; they are not physical memory-model proofs or native acceptance. Exact setup and header bytes must bind this producer before the changed candidate can be investigated; no historical timeout resolution or full SMP correctness is asserted.

Retain GNU GCC, SMP, multiple VMs and multiple threaded VMs, CPU-adaptive concurrency, the original 600-second whole deadline and all historical failures. A seeded runtime is not a completed producer. Full two-pass bootstrap and source closure must independently pass before producer export. Frame admission assumes serialized lifecycle ownership and GNU atomic semantics; bounded models do not prove arbitrary-width counters, incarnation reuse, root discovery, physical ordering or unbounded liveness. Growth/startup callback behavior, legacy void-cleanup reporting, caller/VM lifetime and concurrent host cleanup remain source/native obligations. Only official loader and FFI fixtures are permitted: no RTLD_NEXT injection or private cleanup invocation. Complete GSC, stress, fault paths, GC/FFI, Gerbil and performance gates remain OPEN until exact-source native receipts qualify them.
